Sonoma Zinfandel.title: Seghesio Sonoma Zinfandel 2024
Sonoma Zinfandel.originAndGrape: USA › Sonoma County · 87% Zinfandel, 7% Petite Sirah, 1% Syrah, 1% Carignane, 1% Mataro, and 3% mixed reds. Lots from Russian River, Dry Creek, Alexander, and Sonoma valleys. 55% estate fruit.
Sonoma Zinfandel.tastingNotes: Black raspberry, mixed berry pie, and baking spice, with a brambly edge and pliable tannin. Bold and richly fruited, with a lift of acidity on the finish.
Sonoma Zinfandel.vintageNote: A cooler, even-paced 2024 season after a wet winter. Crisp, freshly picked fruit and a lift of acidity against the wine's usual warmth.
Sonoma Zinfandel.similarTo: Classic Sonoma County Zinfandel. Ripe and spicy, not a jammy Central Valley style.
Sonoma Zinfandel.idealPairings: Dutch oven short-rib braises, Thanksgiving turkey with sausage stuffing or cranberry, and spicy chili broths.

Chateauneuf-du-Pape.title: Kirkland Signature Châteauneuf-du-Pape 2024, Cuvée du Terroir des Papes
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.originAndGrape: France › Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Southern Rhône · 70% Grenache, 10% Syrah, 10% Mourvèdre, and 10% Cinsault.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.arbitrage: Costco private label created by Guillaume Gonnet, a third-generation Châteauneuf winemaker. Cuvée du Terroir des Papes has been the name since the 2018 vintage, when Gonnet took over from Domaine de Nalys (those earlier bottles were labeled Cuvée de Nalys). Contract bottled by Invinova for SAS Gonnet Gilson, not estate bottled. Usually around $20 at Costco.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.tastingNotes: Red and black fruit, thyme and garrigue, licorice, and a savory olive note. Generous and dry, with fine tannin and a grippy, savory finish.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.vintageNote: Very young. The 2024 is more fruit-forward and less tannic than the prior vintage, and it opens with air. Fine to pour tonight if you decant.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.similarTo: A generous, modern-leaning village Châteauneuf. Grenache-led Southern Rhône, not a tannic old-school cellar bomb.
Chateauneuf-du-Pape.idealPairings: Seared lamb chops, herb-roasted turkey and mushroom gravy, and Dutch oven braises.

Napa Sauvignon Blanc.title: Groth Napa Valley Sauvignon Blanc
Napa Sauvignon Blanc.originAndGrape: USA › Napa Valley · Sauvignon Blanc with Sémillon (recent releases 89% / 11%). Fruit from the family's Oakville estate and other Napa sites. The Sémillon is estate-grown.
Napa Sauvignon Blanc.tastingNotes: Cantaloupe, lime, and citrus oil, with a touch of white pepper. Smooth and a little waxy from neutral-oak sur lie aging, then a crisp, clean finish.
Napa Sauvignon Blanc.similarTo: Napa Sauvignon Blanc in a richer, Bordeaux-white register, not a grassy New Zealand style.
Napa Sauvignon Blanc.idealPairings: Poached shrimp or white fish, lemony starters, and roast turkey white meat.

Sauternes.title: Château Suduiraut 2023
Sauternes.originAndGrape: France › Preignac, Sauternes · 100% Sémillon in 2023, from botrytis-affected grapes. Premier Cru Classé en 1855. 91-hectare estate on gravelly, sandy-clay soils next to Château d'Yquem. The vineyard is planted to 80% Sémillon, 15% Sauvignon Blanc, and 5% Sauvignon Gris. AXA Millésimes since 1992.
Sauternes.tastingNotes: Peach, mirabelle, verbena, and a little wood spice, then baked apple, candied citron, bergamot, and gingerbread. Dense and fresh, with a velvety texture and a long, smooth finish.
Sauternes.vintageNote: The 2023 is generous, with distinct acidity and a classic botrytised character, plus fresh and candied citrus. The estate likens it to 2021. This vintage is 100% Sémillon.
Sauternes.similarTo: A citrus-fresh, pure-Sémillon Premier Cru Sauternes. Opulent but not heavy, not a simple late-harvest sweet wine.
Sauternes.idealPairings: Pumpkin or pecan pie, blue cheese, and a glass on its own after dinner.
